Theme

# Philosophy quotes about dignity

Dignity names the worth that persons claim simply as persons—and the respect that worth demands.

18 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Kantian and rights-based ethics make dignity central; other traditions speak of face, honor, or Buddha-nature. Politics asks how institutions honor or violate dignity.

## In the history of philosophy

From Stoic cosmopolitanism and Confucian respect to modern human rights, dignity bridges ethics and law.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Blaise Pascal](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/blaise-pascal) , [Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [John Stuart Mill](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-stuart-mill) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Mencius](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mencius) , [Mary Wollstonecraft](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/mary-wollstonecraft) , [Qian Mu](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/qian-mu)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is dignity in philosophy?

It is the intrinsic or status-based worth of persons that grounds respect and limits on treatment.

### Is dignity the same as honor?

Honor is often social and hierarchical; dignity is frequently claimed as equal and inalienable—though histories intertwine.
